item.title: The hypocrisy of Mikel Arteta’s scathing reaction towards ‘kid’ Max Dowman
item.description: They don’t call them the troubled teens for no reason. Max Dowman is 16 years of age (not sure anybody’s mentioned that before). Arsenal ’s child prodigy is one of football’s most exciting talents, though as someone who cannot yet legally drive, he is still some way off reaching full maturity. His straight red card against Fleetwood , born from the short fuse not uncommon in those his age, was a clear indication of that. His outburst was hardly unprovoked; Fleetwood midfielder Harrison Neal had just lunged in with a scissoring challenge, the type that has broken legs before. But that isn’t an excuse to lose your head, not at this level. Neither is his age, which on the pitch is a non-factor; he has been entrusted to play senior football so is expected to carry himself like a senior footballer. Max Dowman was sent off for violent conduct against Fleetwood (Reuters) Dowman’s kick-out, even if soft, was a major blunder on his end. He is now suspended for three games - barring a successful appeal - and will not get an opportunity for redemption until the visit of Manchester City on 29 November. That’s over a month of unavailability. He should receive a dressing down from his manager to drive home the lesson that needs to be learned, especially in the context of his sending off for the England U19s at the beginning of the month. There is a pattern emerging of ill-discipline that Arsenal need to nip in the bud. However, there’s a good way of dealing with these things and a bad way, especially when the player in question is not yet an adult. Mikel Arteta went for the latter when he appeared direct a furious reaction towards Dowman from the touchline as he walked down the tunnel, for all the world to see. This has now become the story, arguably more than his red card. To reiterate, Arteta had every right to be angry at his player. The sending off was stupid, petulant and completely avoidable, putting Arsenal at a man disadvantage for the final five minutes, during which they could have found a late winner and avoided the perils of penalties. It lit the blue-touch paper for Arsenal’s humiliating Carabao Cup exit that would be sealed 21 minutes later. But to put him on blast so publicly rather than wait until they’ve got the privacy of the dressing room felt irresponsible. Dowman is in an especially unique position as a player who burst onto the scene at the very top level aged just 15. Arteta himself has repeatedly stated how careful the club have to be in nurturing him to his full potential. After becoming the Premier League’s youngest ever scorer with his goal against Everton in March, Arteta was keen to ensure the noise surrounding Dowman didn’t become overwhelming, even telling the media: “I need your help with that, guys.” You haven’t helped yourself here, Mikel. item.title: Bills pass rush gets a golden opportunity against battered Ravens line
item.description: ORCHARD PARK - Whether or not star quarterback Lamar Jackson is back in time to face the Buffalo Bills Sunday at Highmark Stadium , one of the biggest keys for the Baltimore Ravens will be the performance of its injury-ravaged offensive line. Obviously, getting Jackson on the field gives the line a better chance to look good because he’s such a dynamic player both as a passer and runner, similar to Josh Allen in that he can turn a potential sack into a 30-yard scramble or completion. Still, the Bills’ defensive front has to take advantage of Baltimore’s blockers who have already used 16 different five-man combinations in the first seven games, plus lost brutish blocking tight end Durham Smythe for the season. With their line struggling to find consistency amid all the turnover, the Ravens’ offense has been haphazard. Sure, they topped 30 points three times, but those games came against the defenses of the Falcons, Cowboys and Colts that currently rank 20th, 23rd and 24th, respectively, in points allowed per game. They managed a mundane 24 points (with Jackson) in a win over the lowly Titans, and in the other three games, losses to the Saints (with Jackson), Browns and Bengals (without Jackson), they’ve scored a total of just 40 points. “It’s like, what are we asking some of these younger guys to do? Can they do it? Can we be good at the things that we’re asking them to do?” Ravens coach Jesse Minter said of the offensive line. “We’ve certainly had a little bit of flux on the O-line, but that’s not an excuse to say that we shouldn’t be able to move the ball with who we have.” How Ravens offensive line injuries have hurt Baltimore's offense Who they have, of course, is maybe Jackson, running back Derrick Henry, and wide receiver Zay Flowers, three of the best players at their positions in the NFL. But when your line is struggling to protect and create gaps in the run game, an offense can get bogged down. Things only got trickier in the 35-13 loss to Cincinnati last week when the line suffered another setback as rookie first-round pick Vega Ioane hurt his knee and is likely out against Buffalo. Veteran center Cam Jurgens, who was acquired in a trade from the Eagles, made his Ravens’ debut against the Bengals and was average while RT Roger Rosengarten and LG John Simpson both had rough games. “Sure, but that’s no excuse,” LT Ronnie Stanley said of the injuries. “We have a lot of players hurt; they have players hurt. That’s happened throughout the league. We still have enough to get the job done, and that’s what we expect from our players.” Through seven games, even though both Jackson and backup QB Tyler Huntley are mobile and can escape pressure, the Ravens’ sack percentage against of 8.2% is seventh-worst. item.title: Dirk Kuyt takes interim charge of Fenerbahce ahead of Liverpool reunion
item.description: Dirk Kuyt takes interim charge of Fenerbahce ahead of Liverpool reunion Dirk Kuyt has been placed in interim charge of Fenerbahce , setting up a touchline reunion with Liverpool when the Reds visit Turkiye in the Champions League next week. The Dutchman steps up after Ismail Kartal resigned as head coach earlier this week. Kuyt had joined Kartal's staff as assistant manager during the summer. Kartal stepped down after defeat to arch-rivals Galatasaray on Monday night left Fenerbahce fifth in the table. Fenerbahce have not named a permanent successor. The club said Kuyt will lead the team "until a new head coach is appointed". The 46-year-old is a popular figure at Fenerbahce, where he scored 37 goals in 130 games, winning the Süper Lig title in 2014. A familiar face for Liverpool Kuyt had signed for Fenerbahce from Liverpool after six seasons at Anfield, between 2006 and 2012. He scored 71 goals in 285 appearances for the Reds. After retiring from football in 2017, Kuyt has stepped into coaching. He's had senior roles with ADO Den Haag, Beerschot and FC Dordrecht before returning to Fenerbahce as assistant in the summer. Unless a permanent appointment is made prior, Kuyt will be in the opposition dugout when Liverpool face Fenerbahce on Wednesday, November 4, in their fourth match of the Champions League league phase. Liverpool have a perfect record after three games, while Fenerbahce are winless. The Turkish side have drawn twice and lost once.

item.title: NC State & Baylor should make high-profile coaching hires
item.description: Over the last decade, thanks to the transfer portal and NIL money, college football has become a sport with its own economy. Money drives everything in college football. The goal is to spend as much money as possible on the roster so it has the most talent. This shift has also changed how head coaches are viewed, because would you rather spend money on a good head coach or on players? It becomes a bit of a “chicken or the egg” situation. If you pay a good head coach, he may be able to bring in better players and get the most out of them. Or, you can cut out the middleman and just pay for good players. This also changes the economy around firing head coaches. MORE: Biggest risers in College Football after Week 8 Massive contract buyouts The ACC Huddle pregame show kicks off on the campus of Florida State University and features former FSU head coach Jimbo Fisher. Several fans in the background hold signs reading “bring back Jimbo” and “some legends hit different.” Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) We’ve seen some head coaches with massive contract buyouts (Brian Kelly and Jimbo Fisher, to name a few), but we’ve also seen schools hesitate to fire head coaches because of them. Because if you have to pay $20 million to buy out a head coach, you would get more return on your money to just invest that $20 million on the roster. Well, in the last week, NC State and Baylor got tired of waiting. NC State fired head coach Dave Doeren in his 14th season on the job, and owes him in the neighborhood of $10 million in a buyout. Dave Aranda won a Big 12 Championship at Baylor, but that goodwill ran out as he was just fired and is reportedly owed $12 million. Both schools now have a job opening for head coach, and both are rumored to have interesting plans to fill them. Kartal resigned on Tuesday, less than 24 hours after the Istanbul derby defeat against Galatasaray. Kuyt first task will be a league match against Göztepe on Saturday. If he's still in charge after that, he will face his former club Liverpool in the Champions League next Wednesday. item.title: Michael Carrick and Bruno Fernandes take major step in bid to salvage Man United crisis
item.description: Michael Carrick and Bruno Fernandes have held clear-the-air talks as the Manchester United manager and captain try to rebuild their relationship. Fernandes was critical of Carrick’s tactics, and the team’s lack of pressing, in United’s 4-1 defeat to Como last week . And four days later the reigning PFA Player of the Year was dropped from the team and left unused as a substitute during the 3-0 loss to Bournemouth, with Carrick describing his omission as a “pure football” decision. Michael Carrick and Bruno Fernandes have held clear-the-air talks (PA Archive) But whereas Sunday seemed to signal the end of Carrick’s reign, United instead decided against sacking the 45-year-old and he will be in charge for Saturday’s trip to Chelsea . He and Fernandes spoke at United’s Carrington training ground on Tuesday in a conversation which could pave the way for the Portugal international to return to the team. Fernandes is deemed to have been back to the best version of himself in the last couple of days after a tough two weeks. But he has failed to find form this season and has not scored in his last seven appearances, while his only Premier League goals came in August, when he scored a hat-trick against Ipswich. Carrick preferred to pick summer signing Youri Tielemans and Mason Mount instead of Fernandes for the Bournemouth game.

item.title: Thierry Henry clarifies his Lamine Yamal comments after Ballon d’Or criticism
item.description: Spain and Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal speaks after winning the Trophy for the Men's Young Talent of the Year during the 2026 Ballon d'Or France Football award ceremony at the Palladium Theatre in London on October 26, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Thierry Henry has clarified his comments after coming in for some criticism for a question directed at Lamine Yamal during Monday’s Ballon d’Or ceremony. Yamal picked up the Kopa Trophy for the third time , with Henry asking the teenager: “That’s your third one, right? But is it the one that you really wanted tonight?” The comments did not go down well with some people and Henry has now responded in a post on social media. “I want to clarify some stuff as some people got really excited for actually nothing. With Lamine Yamal, it wasn’t about checking his ego at all. I simply thought that, since it was the third time he had won that trophy, I was just asking him if it was the one he truly wanted,” he said. “We all knew what he wanted. Unfortunately, he didn’t get it. I’m a big fan of Lamine Yamal. I wasn’t checking his ego at all. If you don’t like the joke, I can understand that. But please, don’t do that; he really is one of those players I will pay to watch—I love him. “I was just asking him if it was the one he really wants, because I knew the real prize was coming after —which, unfortunately, he didn’t win. He’s a hell of a player; I love watching him, and I would pay to see him play.”

item.title: Barcelona dressing room remains united despite back-to-back defeats to PSG and Madrid
item.description: Barcelona dressing room remains united despite back-to-back defeats to PSG and Madrid Barcelona’s senior players have organised a team barbecue at the Ciutat Esportiva Joan Gamper in an effort to reinforce squad unity following consecutive defeats to Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, according to SPORT . The initiative comes at a difficult moment for Hansi Flick’s side, but the report indicates that the recent results have not damaged relationships within the dressing room. The Catalan club has lost two major fixtures in quick succession , leaving the players frustrated with their performances. Nevertheless, the squad remains united and recognises the need to improve on the pitch as Barcelona look to regain momentum in the coming matches. Barcelona captains organise barbecue to strengthen unity The team gathering is scheduled for Wednesday after training and a commercial photo shoot involving several players. Barcelona dressing room is united despite back-to-back defeats. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) The squad will then share a barbecue at the club’s training complex, giving teammates an opportunity to spend time together away from their usual footballing responsibilities. The decision to hold the event at the Ciutat Esportiva Joan Gamper also offers greater privacy. Previous team lunches at restaurants around Barcelona have attracted journalists and curious onlookers, prompting the players to choose a more discreet setting for this occasion. Now, with fixture congestion to look forward to and pressure mounting after the recent losses, maintaining strong relationships within the squad remains an important part of the team’s response. Barcelona dressing room remains positive Barcelona captains have organised a team gathering. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The defeats have undoubtedly disappointed the players, particularly because they came against two major opponents within the space of a week. Barcelona’s performances have exposed areas that require improvement , and the squad understands the importance of returning to winning ways. However, there are no internal problems coming from the results. The relationships between teammates remain strong, while the players continue to trust the work being carried out under Flick. Simply put, frustration over results does not necessarily indicate divisions within a dressing room, and the atmosphere suggests Barcelona’s players are treating the setbacks as a collective responsibility.

item.title: Kobbie Mainoo returns to Man United training ahead of Chelsea clash
item.description: Kobbie Mainoo returns to Man United training ahead of Chelsea clash Kobbie Mainoo is said to have returned to Manchester United training after a four-match absence, putting the midfielder in contention for Saturday’s trip to Chelsea. Mainoo’s injury timeline Mainoo completed United’s 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur on 10 October but sustained an issue during the match. The injury then ruled him out of the Champions League defeat at Atletico Madrid three days later. Head coach Michael Carrick was unsure whether the midfielder would recover for the meeting with Leeds United, which Mainoo subsequently missed. Carrick then estimated on 20 October that the academy graduate could require another 10 days (via RotoWire ). Mainoo remained unavailable for the matches against Como and Bournemouth. Wednesday return gives Carrick a Chelsea selection option Mainoo’s return was confirmed in an update which stated: “The midfielder took part in Wednesday morning’s session at Carrington after missing United’s last four matches through injury” (via Sam C ). Mainoo’s reaction to the session is likely to influence whether he starts, makes the bench or is held back at Stamford Bridge. The timing could prove useful for Carrick, who will remain in charge against Chelsea despite United sitting 16th in the Premier League. His side have won only twice in 12 matches across all competitions this season. Carrick began the campaign with Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos as his central pairing before Mainoo replaced Santos. Carlos Baleba has also recently returned to full fitness following an ankle injury, giving the coach more scope to adjust a midfield which has struggled to provide enough creativity and drive. From United’s academy to an FA Cup final goal Mainoo played for Cheadle & Gatley before joining Manchester United’s academy in 2014 at the age of nine. No transfer fee was involved. He made his senior debut against Charlton Athletic in the League Cup on 10 January 2023. Before his latest injury absence, he had accumulated 110 competitive appearances for the Red Devils and scored eight goals. The midfielder won the FA Youth Cup in 2022 and lifted the senior FA Cup two years later. Mainoo scored United’s second goal in the 2-1 final victory over Manchester City at Wembley. He has never left the club on loan and committed his long-term future to United in April 2026 by signing a contract running until June 2031. Provided Mainoo suffers no reaction in training, a place on the bench against Chelsea appears the most likely cautious route back into Carrick’s side. Final Thoughts Mainoo returned to team training on Wednesday after missing four matches. The midfielder is now in contention for Saturday’s visit to Chelsea. item.title: John Wall reveals the ‘trigger point’ that led to Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum’s beef
item.description: Photo by Jonathan Bachman/Getty Images Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum’s relationship falling apart has become one of the biggest talking points of the NBA season. Brown and Tatum were once one of the most formidable duos in the NBA, leading the Boston Celtics to five Eastern Conference Finals, two NBA Finals, and an NBA championship in 2024. However, the last few years have seen their relationship collapse, as their individual rises to superstardom got in the way of their friendship. John Wall says Jayson Tatum’s return from Achilles injury led to friction with Jaylen Brown In an interview with Ashley Nicole Moss of Complex, former NBA All-Star John Wall discussed the issues Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum had with each other that led to their partnership collapsing. He believes that Brown getting to experience playing without Tatum, only to be sidelined when Tatum returned, made a huge difference. In particular, Brown no longer getting the distinction of being announced last in the starting lineup when Tatum returned showed him that Tatum will always be considered the superstar. Wall said: “Everybody thought Boston was going to be on a rebuild last year, and the way Jaylen Brown played got them there. Now Tatum comes back, and it’s like, ‘Okay, Tatum’s playing well, but he’s not playing at his All-Star level, MVP level.’ “So now, is Jaylen Brown taking a back seat? Like, even he said, the first game when Tatum came back, Jaylen Brown was getting called out last every game of the season. “Now Tatum’s back, he goes back to second-to-last. It be those little triggering points that make people, like, go against it. I think that’s when Boston started realising, like, somebody got to go, and it ain’t going to be Tatum.” For years, the belief had been that the Celtics value Jayson Tatum more than Jaylen Brown as the main superstar of the franchise. Even after Jaylen Brown won Finals MVP en route to the 2024 NBA Championship, the Celtics seemingly valued Tatum more, with the former Duke standout getting the biggest contract in NBA history at the time, just a year after Brown got a similar deal. Now, Brown and Tatum are rivals in the Eastern Conference, playing for two of the most historic franchises and hoping to get back to the NBA Finals. item.title: Ludlow cancels third meeting since summer drought
item.description: Ludlow Racecourse is also home to Ludlow Golf Club [Genevieve Tudor - BBC Radio Shropshire] Ludlow has been forced to cancel a third successive jumps meeting in the 2026-27 season because of the hard ground conditions caused by the summer drought. Grass has died in certain key areas of the course and managing director Simon Sherwood admits that they "are in the lap of the Gods" as to exactly how long the re-seeding process will take as it will need not only rain, but sun too. As one of the best naturally draining racecourses in the country, which normally loses very few meetings during the harsher winter months, it had already been anticipated that Ludlow might not start the season on time. And the first scheduled meeting on 15 October was switched instead to Worcester, 35 miles away. Ludlow also lost the racing scheduled for last week, and has now cancelled the Farmers meeting on 5 November. Their next meeting is now planned for Monday, 23 November. Dry summer puts horse racing season under threat Five big Welsh hopes for the National Hunt season One of the Shropshire track's alternative summer uses is as a weekend Caravan Club site [Ged Scott - BBC Sport] "We're on very much a gravel base at Ludlow Racecourse," Sherwood told BBC Radio Shropshire. "It's a fantastic racecourse when we have a wet winter. People love sending their horses to us as the ground never gets too deep for the horses. "But it can be a bit of a nightmare when we have the other extreme, which obviously we did this summer - the worst since I've been here." Former national hunt racing jockey Sherwood, who rode Desert Orchid to victory in the 1989 Cheltenham Gold Cup, took over as clerk of the course from long-serving Grand National winner Bob Davies in 2019. He said this summer - the driest since 1976 - had been hard to handle. "We had no rain at all in July and the average temperature every day was 31 degrees. "The grass effectively goes to sleep. It went yellow. It goes into a dormant state to survive. Just as it does in people's back gardens at home." Simon Sherwood rode one of British horseracing's most famous horses, Desert Orchard, winning the Cheltenham Gold Cup in 1989 [Shutterstock] He continued: "We don't have the water to keep watering as we have to pull it out of the River Corve to supplement what we can get from the reservoir and, at that time of year, there are restrictions. We had to sit and suffer until the rain came again. "It was not until about September time that the grass started to wake up again. "They did well so we have to give them credit, but I think (it) was about us not being on our level, we need to do better. item.title: One World Series stat shows why Tampa Bay Rays’ Game 4 win might not be nearly enough
item.description: Photo by Julio Aguilar/Getty Images The Tampa Bay Rays might have just picked up one of the most impressive World Series wins ever, but it may not be enough. Going into the bottom of the 12th inning, the Milwaukee Brewers were only three outs away from winning their first World Series championship. They didn’t manage to get a single one of those outs, though, as the Rays scored two runs to claim a 4-3 victory. The win was incredibly impressive, something which hasn’t been done in the MLB postseason in well over a decade. Tampa Bay became one of a handful of teams to stave off elimination in an extra inning despite being down heading into it. But of all the stats currently being discussed, one should worry them more than any other. No MLB team in history has forced Game 6 in the World Series after going down 3-0 In any sport, everyone knows that going down 3-0 means that the series is more or less over. Baseball has seen it just once, when the Boston Red Sox did it in the ALCS. So despite the fact that their Game 4 win was excellent for morale, the Rays are still facing an incredibly difficult challenge. In fact, there is one historical statistic which shows that they will have to make history to even keep their title hopes alive any further, something which is far easier said than done. “There have been 25 teams in World Series history that have taken a 3 game to 0 lead,” MLB writer Bob Nightengale shared on X. “Only 4 of those teams lost Game 4 to even force a Game 5. No one has forced a Game 6, let alone a Game 7.” That means the Rays would make history even if they can just manage to win again on Wednesday. The Brewers are in a commanding position and it is difficult to see them losing this series. One way or the other, history will be made in Game 5 of the 2026 World Series. item.title: Why did Fleetwood have to lose player for Arsenal penalty shootout?
item.description: Fleetwood Town were forced to drop down to 10 men for their EFL Cup penalty shootout against Arsenal on Tuesday [Getty Images] Fleetwood Town were forced to surrender a player for their penalty shootout win over Arsenal at Highbury on Tuesday night. The Fishermen beat the Gunners 5-3 on penalties to book their place in the EFL Cup quarter-finals for the first time in the club's history. But as the two sides entered the shootout following a 1-1 draw in 90 minutes, the hosts were forced to elect a player to sit out. This is because teams are forced to play penalty shootouts with the same number of players involved on either side. Arsenal ended the match with 10 men after teenager Max Dowman was shown a red card in the second half. Law 10.3 of the International Football Association Board's laws of the game states that "if at the end of the match and before or during the kicks one team has a greater number of players than its opponents, it must reduce its numbers to the same number as its opponents and the referee must be informed of the name and number of each player excluded. Any excluded player is not eligible to take part in the kicks". This includes goalkeepers defending the penalties. Fleetwood named defender Jake Batty as the player to miss out on taking part in the shootout so the two sides were even. "Fleetwood have to nominate a player to not take a penalty and that is Jake Batty because of Dowman's sending off, so it becomes 10 against 10," Sky Sports commentator Peter Drury explained at the time. Saturday’s 2-0 defeat was only Spurs’ second win at Stamford Bridge in 36 years, and maybe more worrying for Alonso was the form of goalkeeper Mike Penders, who struggled on his first Premier League start. The competition has certainly opened up following League Two Fleetwood Town’s shock win over Premier League champions Arsenal, and this competition could give Chelsea the chance to claim their first domestic silverware since 2018. item.title: Indiana center Bray Lynch on Josh Hoover’s play, toughness: ‘He’s a dog like that’
item.description: ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 24: Josh Hoover #10 of the Indiana Hoosiers plays against the Michigan Wolverines at Michigan Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover made an impression on his teammates the moment he arrived in Bloomington this past offseason. Just ask Bray Lynch, the center he’s taken snaps from all season. Lynch said he was unsurprised by Hoover’s drive to play through an arm injury against Ohio State and Michigan, saying that if he’d been asked back in the preseason if Hoover would do such a thing his response would be a simple “hell yeah.” “He’s a dog like that,” Lynch said. “You saw it in spring ball, you see it in the weight room and you see it now on Saturdays.” Hoover’s shown his toughness multiple times throughout the season, staying in for the Hoosiers’ season opener against North Texas despite blood pouring down his face from a nose injury he suffered after his facemask was grabbed. He’s even ran in to try and throw a few blocks for Turbo Richard and Lee Beebe Jr. during critical runs, namely against Northwestern. Then came the Michigan game when Hoover battled through the aforementioned injury, ultimately delivering in overtime with a pass to tight end Brock Schott before diving into the endzone himself for the go ahead touchdown that ended up winning the day. One thing that’s clear about Hoover is this: he’s more than earned the trust and respect of his teammates despite this being his first and only season in Bloomington. They’re willing to fight for him in the same way he is for them. “We have full confidence in him,” Lynch said. “We knew that when the time arose to make a play, he was gonna find a way to get it done.” Join the conversation! Instead of playing it safe, Heyward wanted to run a traditional play. He didn’t want any part of the victory formation. “Get rid of that. item.title: 'I promise': Mikel Brown Jr. has a message for Nets fans after going from hero to zero vs Celtics
item.description: Photo by Dustin Satloff/Getty Images Mikel Brown Jr. must have experienced a rollercoaster of emotions during the Brooklyn Nets’ heartbreaking defeat against the Boston Celtics. The 20-year-old is in his rookie season in the NBA, and his performances so far have shown that there is a lot to like about his game. Against the Boston Celtics, Brown became the hero at the end of regulation time, but everything came crashing down in the final moments of the game. Mikel Brown Jr. makes a promise to Brooklyn Nets fans after losing to Boston Celtics The game between the Brooklyn Nets and the Boston Celtics was an absolute thriller. The Nets were losing at the end of regulation time, but Brown pulled off a clutch three-pointer with 0.2 seconds left on the clock to send the game to overtime. The rookie was the hero in that moment, but the tables turned at the end of overtime, as his mistakes cost the Nets the win. Brown missed two layups in the final six seconds of the game, when his side were leading. Instead of slowing the game down and drawing an intentional foul, he drove into traffic and missed a contested layup over Paul George. The Celtics secured the rebound and called a timeout. Then, in the final action of the game, Jayson Tatum scored at the buzzer to win it. That became a hero-to-zero moment in a short space of time for young Brown, but he showed extreme maturity after the game by taking accountability for his actions. He tweeted : “That one is on me, Brooklyn! I’m going to shake back. I promise y’all that.” Even in his post-match interviews, Brown put the blame on himself and admitted that his decision-making should’ve been better. He said, as per Brian Lewis of the New York Post on X : “It’s a broken play. I blame me. “We weren’t supposed to switch that and I switched it. Made a couple of mistakes down the stretch that hurt us. So I’m going to take the blame for it, learn from it and get prepared for the next game.” Such accountability from such a young man is great to see. We’re sure Brown will learn from his mistakes and bounce back in the coming games. item.title: The Sheffield United Dilemma Chris Wilder Surely Can’t Ignore
item.description: The Sheffield United Dilemma Chris Wilder Surely Can’t Ignore When Romelle Donovan arrived at Sheffield United on loan from Brentford during the summer transfer window, there was genuine excitement surrounding the 19-year-old winger. The young Englishman had shown enough promise to suggest that he could become an exciting addition to Chris Wilder’s squad, but he also arrived with a considerable challenge ahead of him. Donovan was tasked with filling the void left by boyhood Blade Andre Brooks, who departed Bramall Lane to join Norwich City. Replacing a homegrown talent who had developed a connection with the supporters was never going to be straightforward, but the Brentford youngster appeared to possess the attributes to make his own mark in S2. His pre-season performances offered plenty of encouragement, and he showed further glimpses of his potential during the opening weeks of the campaign. Yet, as the season has progressed, Donovan has found himself spending far more time watching from the sidelines than making a meaningful contribution on the pitch. And that is becoming increasingly difficult for Sheffield United supporters to understand. Only Wilder knows precisely why the teenager has been overlooked so frequently, but the decision to leave him out of the starting eleven has become a frustrating talking point among the Blades faithful. With United struggling to find consistency and a reliable attacking threat, the continued absence of a player who appears capable of injecting some much-needed energy into the side is raising legitimate questions. (Photo by George Wood/Getty Images) There is a reason why Donovan’s appearances, however brief, have generated excitement among the supporters. He plays with an aggression, directness and willingness to take defenders on that can sometimes be missing from United’s attacking play.
